_comment: Which hull each retail class stands on and paths with, recovered 2026-09-20 by four
independent opencode walks over vampire.dll (setter-out, table-down, per-class spawn chain,
and a byte-level tie-break). See docs/vtmb/navigation-jump-links.md, section 'The two hull
A CONSTRUCTOR writes the hull, which is why the kernel ledger -- which does not record
constructor accesses -- saw a witnessed store for almost nobody. The stores below were found
by scanning .text for the displacements 68 15 00 00 / 6c 15 00 00; a parallel scan for
lea/add/sub against those offsets finds none, so the set is exhaustive.
`standing` is m_eHull (+0x1568): it sizes the collision box through SetHullSizeNormal and
every trace/LoS helper takes its extents from it. `pathing` is +0x156c, which has no datamap
record and is never saved: CAI_Navigator::SetGoal caches it at 0x102ecd2c and the whole A*
family feeds it to CAI_Node::GetPosition. So the Recast agent follows `pathing` and the
ORDER MATTERS: most-derived first. A class with no row of its own inherits from the nearest
ancestor that has one, and the runtime resolves that by taking the first row whose class is in
the body's retail chain. CNPC_VRat is the case that needs it -- it has no constructor of its
own, and its value comes from CNPC_VScurrying's.
Slot 337 GetUsedHullBits is a PRECACHE declaration, not the stand hull. The values coincide
for most species, which is exactly the trap; only a witnessed write counts.

rows.note: CNPC_VRat has no constructor of its own; its factory 0x103ad710 runs this one and re-vtables.
Writes +0x1568 alone. Stands on SHERIFF_HULL and routes on the human mesh, so he needs no agent of his own.
The inverse split: human-sized box, HENGEYOKAI pathing. A transform later raises standing to 18 and leaves pathing alone (0x1038096e) -- 0002's, listed under 0018's Seams.
Settled by the byte-level tie-break: 0x103b6d27 b8 0a 00 00 00 feeds both stores. A reading of 0xb is HeadClaw's value.
Written in Spawn, not the constructor: it overrides the inherited 0/0.
Spawn-time store of the value it already inherited.
Zeroes both before any derived constructor runs, which is what rescues the base sentinel below.

23 is one past the 22-row table -- an unassigned value, not a sentinel row. It never survives construction, and would fault if it reached a reader: the accessors index the pointer table raw, with no bounds check anywhere.
